The African Development Bank Group has approved a $102m financing package for Sterling Bank Nigeria Limited to expand access to credit for small and medium-sized enterprises, women and youth-led businesses, and vulnerable farming communities across Nigeria. The facility is expected to support at least 200 businesses, create up to 6,000 jobs and provide financial assistance to more than 5,000 smallholder farmers affected by insecurity, displacement and climate-related challenges. According to a statement issued by the AfDB on Tuesday, the financing package combines long-term credit, sustainable financing, concessional agricultural loans and trade guarantees to address funding constraints facing Nigerian businesses. The statement read, “The Board of Directors of the African Development Bank Group has approved a $102m financing package for Sterling Bank Nigeria Limited to expand access to finance for small and medium-sized enterprises, women and youth-led businesses, businesses pursuing sustainable green and social investments, and vulnerable farming communities across Nigeria.” The bank disclosed that the $102m package comprises a $50m line of credit, a $20m sustainable loan, a $2m concessional loan under its Agri-Food SME Catalytic Financing Mechanism and a $30m Trade Finance Transaction Guarantee. The $50m credit facility will provide competitively priced long-term financing to businesses operating in priority sectors, including healthcare, education, agriculture, renewable energy and transportation. The $2m concessional component will support vulnerable agricultural communities through the Sterling Affordable Microlending Programme, implemented in collaboration with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees. The programme is expected to assist more than 5,000 smallholder farmers and agricultural SMEs in rebuilding their livelihoods and strengthening resilience against economic and environmental shocks. The $20m sustainable loan will support qualifying green and social projects under Sterling Bank’s Sustainable Financing Framework. Similarly, the $30m trade finance guarantee is expected to facilitate up to $150m in trade transactions, enabling Nigerian businesses to access new markets and participate in regional and international supply chains. Commenting on the approval, the AfDB’s Acting Vice President for Regional Development, Integration and Business Delivery and Director General for Nigeria, Abdul Kamara, said, “A vibrant private sector is critical to Nigeria’s economic transformation, but different businesses face different financing challenges. This package reflects the African Development Bank’s understanding that there is no one-size-fits-all solution. “By combining financing for SMEs, women- and youth-led enterprises, vulnerable farming communities, sustainable investments, and trade, we are helping more Nigerian businesses access the capital they need to grow, create jobs and contribute to economic development. The operation also supports two of the Bank’s Four Cardinal Points: harnessing demographic transformation for economic development and mobilising capital for inclusive and sustainable growth.” The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Sterling Bank, Abubakar Suleiman, welcomed the financing arrangement, describing it as an opportunity to strengthen productive businesses. “Nigeria’s long-term economic growth will depend significantly on our ability to strengthen the productive capacity of local businesses and ensure that financing reaches sectors with the greatest potential to create jobs and improve livelihoods,” Suleiman said. He explained that the partnership would help address financing gaps affecting SMEs, women entrepreneurs, young business owners and underserved communities. The latest approval follows two other AfDB financing packages for Nigerian financial institutions earlier in 2026. These included a $61m package for the Development Bank of Nigeria to support women-led enterprises and a $200m facility for the Bank of Industry to strengthen industrial development and business expansion. Together, the three financing packages amount to $363m in approved support for Nigerian financial institutions this year.
